ask: Users want early, accurate warnings and visibility into context consumption.
plugin: A statusline and monitor read session usage, forecast exhaustion, and notify before the remaining budget becomes unsafe.

ask: Users want long sessions to preserve task state, decisions, and instructions across compaction or clearing.
plugin: PreCompact and SessionStart hooks save a concise working-state ledger and restore it after compaction; a skill keeps that ledger current.

ask: Users want to control when and how conversation context is compressed or cleared.
plugin: Experimental session.measure and session.compact hooks can offer warnings, hold requested compactions, and rewrite compaction instructions or messages; a command provides a guided manual path.

ask: Users want to retain, back up, archive, search, delete, and export local session history on their terms.
plugin: SessionEnd hooks and a bin utility index and back up transcripts, apply configurable retention, and expose archive/search/export commands.

ask: Users want to find, label, link, and navigate sessions and branches easily.
plugin: A command and bin index session metadata, manage stable labels and bookmarks, and provide search across local transcripts and forks.

ask: Users want sessions and memory to survive moving repositories or switching machines.
plugin: A bin tool maps project identities, exports and imports the relevant transcript and memory directories, and checks links before migration.

ask: Users want a reproducible handoff or checkpoint between sessions and collaborators.
plugin: A skill and command generate a concise handoff artifact, save checkpoints, and seed a new session with the relevant context.

ask: Users want project rules and explicit constraints checked before the agent acts.
plugin: A rules skill plus PreToolUse and Stop hooks check proposed edits and final evidence against project instructions, then block or flag violations.

ask: Users want rules, memory, and environment guidance loaded at the right scope and time.
plugin: SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks discover project and user instructions, apply scope filters, and inject a compact verified guidance block.

ask: Users want the agent to stay in the intended worktree and avoid destructive cleanup.
plugin: PreToolUse hooks verify cwd, git branch, and worktree identity before writes or git commands; a monitor warns about active worktree cleanup.

ask: Users want explicit checks before risky Git operations or unapproved file changes.
plugin: PreToolUse hooks inspect commands and diffs, deny unsafe mutations, and require an approved scope ledger before commits or pushes.

ask: Users want parallel sessions to avoid port, file, and ownership collisions.
plugin: An MCP or local monitor maintains a session registry with project locks and port leases, and a hook blocks conflicting writes.

ask: Users want model and reasoning effort chosen or held by task, activity, and session.
plugin: Experimental turn.step and model-switch hooks route model and effort by configurable task rules, with a command for explicit overrides.

ask: Users want the assistant to know the current time, platform, version, and working environment.
plugin: SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks inject fresh local time, repo state, and selected platform facts into context.

ask: Users want local visibility into token spend, limits, and session usage.
plugin: A statusline plus command reads local telemetry and session usage, showing trends, cost, and available quota where the data is exposed.

ask: Users want inspectable events and useful diagnostics for long sessions and failed tools.
plugin: Lifecycle hooks and a monitor write a structured local event journal with latency, tool outcomes, and session identifiers for inspection.

ask: Users want to send feedback without disclosing session contents.
plugin: A command collects an issue summary, previews redactions, and opens or submits a minimal report through GitHub or the configured feedback endpoint.

ask: Users want generated commits and PRs to honor their attribution preference.
plugin: PreToolUse hooks inspect git and GitHub write commands, remove or block unwanted attribution trailers, and audit output.

ask: Users want noisy system context, tool metadata, or redundant reads reduced.
plugin: Experimental prompt.section, tool.describe, and tool.call hooks trim low-value content and surface token-cost warnings.

ask: Users want convenient aliases, completion, and custom commands for common CLI actions.
plugin: A plugin ships namespaced skills and bin helpers for aliases, shell completion, and command wrappers where built-in menus cannot be changed.

ask: Users want clearer, localized, or accessible assistant output.
plugin: An output style and skills set answer format, language, and accessibility rules; a hook can append timestamps or progress cues.

ask: Users want to customize the terminal welcome, spinner, tips, and session status.
plugin: A theme and statusline plugin provides visual customization and can suppress supported UI elements through function hooks.

ask: Users want plugin and MCP installation, state, and health visible from automation.
plugin: A command and monitor query installed plugin and MCP metadata, run health checks, and report actionable status or reauthentication steps.

ask: Users want to start, inspect, or hand off local sessions from other devices and processes.
plugin: A monitor and MCP server keep an opt-in local session registry and expose safe start, attach, and handoff operations through external clients.

ask: Users want durable, observable scheduled tasks and background work.
plugin: A monitor and MCP server maintain job state, enforce one active run per schedule, and report failures and completion to the user.

ask: Users want to add secrets to environment files without exposing the value to the model.
plugin: An MCP tool accepts secret values through a separate user input channel and writes the selected environment file without returning the value to Claude.

ask: Users want reviews, source checks, and proof of completed work before an answer.
plugin: A review agent plus Stop hook checks claims against tool evidence, runs targeted verification, and reports unsupported assertions.

ask: Users want a shareable, portable conversation artifact.
plugin: A command exports selected local transcript turns with redaction and a manifest; an MCP bridge can import the artifact in another client.

ask: Users want Claude Code to use the computer on Windows.
plugin: An MCP server exposes screen inspection, mouse, and keyboard operations through Windows automation APIs.

ask: Users want to provide several pinned code selections as working context.
plugin: An IDE companion and MCP server store named selections and expose them as a tool to Claude Code.

ask: Users want to watch an Appium device while Claude runs mobile tests.
plugin: An MCP server streams device screenshots and Appium actions to a companion viewer during the test workflow.

ask: Users want SSH connections to honor OpenSSH certificate authentication.
plugin: An MCP server delegates SSH sessions to the system OpenSSH client and its existing CertificateFile configuration.

ask: Users want to save a project structure and reuse it in later work.
plugin: A skill and bin command capture a sanitized project scaffold and instantiate it with configurable names and paths.
